paragrafos: **Three measurements side by side, never added together.** Two prediction markets (Polymarket and Kalshi), voting-intention polls checked against the official notice filed with the Commission des sondages, and French press coverage. The first round is on April 18 and the runoff on May 2, 2027.

**On 19/11/2026, the two markets and the polls measure different things about Marine Le Pen.** In the win contract, in the 23:10 UTC reading, Polymarket pays 45.55 and Kalshi 52.00. In the polls with fieldwork up to 17/11, she is first in all 86 first-round lists of the last 45 days, from 8 pollsters, with 27% to 40%, and she leads in the 39 runoff matchups in which she was tested, with 52% to 70%. The two most recent polls in the database, added on 19/11, are YouGov's for Le HuffPost, with fieldwork from 12 to 17/11, and Ifop-Fiducial's for TF1-LCI, Le Figaro and Sud Radio, with fieldwork from 13 to 16/11. Her appeal against ineligibility at the Cour de cassation is due to be decided by early April 2027.

**Jean-Luc Mélenchon is 2nd in the poll average and 3rd in the Polymarket win contract.** In the polls, he averages 18.1 across 47 lists from 7 pollsters over the last 30 days and is among the top two in 80 of the 86 lists of the last 45 days; in the 14 runoff matchups in which he was tested, he trails in all of them, with 30% to 39%. In the win contract, he is at 14.50 on Polymarket and 13.00 on Kalshi.

**Two names in the top five of both markets appear in fewer than half of the lists in the poll database: David Lisnard in 40 of the 86 of the last 45 days, and Christine Lagarde in 2.** Lisnard is 2nd on Polymarket, at 18.05, and at 14.00 on Kalshi; in the polls, he is not among the top two in any of the 40 lists and averages 9.1 across 31 lists from 7 pollsters over the last 30 days. Lagarde is 5th on Polymarket, at 5.20, and at 5.00 on Kalshi; the two lists that test her are from Cluster17 for Politico, with fieldwork on 9 and 10/11, and give her 14% and 8%. Lagarde is not a declared candidate; on 29/10, the European Central Bank announced that she leaves the bank's presidency on 07/02/2027. Teddy Riner, who announced his candidacy on 09/11, is at 1.85 on Polymarket and 1.00 on Kalshi; he appears in 5 of the 86 lists, one from each of 5 pollsters, with 2% to 4.5%; in the two most recent, he has 3% in YouGov's and 4% in Ifop's.

**Édouard Philippe and Raphaël Glucksmann are less than one point apart in the poll average; in the Polymarket win contract, Philippe's price is more than three times Glucksmann's.** Philippe averages 12.5 over the last 30 days, across 33 lists from 7 pollsters, and Glucksmann 11.7, across 46 lists from 7 pollsters; in the lists of the last 45 days in which they appear, Philippe is among the top two in 3 of 60, and Glucksmann in 3 of 81. In the win contract, Philippe is at 5.50 on Polymarket and 5.20 on Kalshi, and Glucksmann at 1.45 and 3.00.

**In the 18:25 UTC press collection of 19/11, three of the ten headlines, from 7 outlets, are about the same announcement by Arcom, the French audiovisual and digital regulator.** For the first time, content creators and influencers will have to follow the pluralism rules during the presidential campaign, like radio and television; the three headlines are from France 24, Libération and franceinfo. Two headlines are about the rapprochement started by Marine Tondelier, of Les Écologistes, with Jean-Luc Mélenchon: Les Echos analyses why she is hastening the party's support for Mélenchon, and Libération reports criticism from Raphaël Glucksmann's camp. On 19/11, Mélenchon told RTL and AFP that the alliance should be able to come together, and Glucksmann told franceinfo that Tondelier, by moving closer to Mélenchon, is moving away from the tradition of Les Écologistes. Les Echos covers Marine Le Pen's proposal to cut public subsidies to associations she calls "politicised", which her rivals criticised in a televised debate. TF1 Info presents Dominique de Villepin as a candidate about to declare; he has called a press conference for 20/11. Villepin appears in 14 of the 86 lists of the last 45 days, with 1% to 3%, and in the win contract he is at 2.15 on Polymarket and 0.90 on Kalshi. Le Parisien reports that Édouard Philippe proposes a five-year suspension of the gradual ban on renting out homes rated as "passoires thermiques", those with the worst energy performance. Le Figaro publishes an analysis of candidates' attempts to bring the war in Ukraine back into the campaign debate, nearly five years after the Russian invasion.

**What this screen does not do.** It does not add or average the two markets, it does not turn a price into a voting intention, and it does not show a poll number without its checked official notice. On the Saturday and Sunday of each round, polls and prices are frozen, as French law of 1977 requires.
